lifecycles._note: Closes the setsecuritygroup + listsecuritygrouprules read-only gaps. The existing 'networking-security-group' lifecycle (scenarios.json) covers create/show/rule-create/rule-show/list-rules/deletes. This fragment: (1) covers setsecuritygroup (PUT /v1/security-groups/{id}) with body {description, loggable} per proven api_docs request_example; (2) covers listsecuritygrouprules by calling GET /v1/security-group-rules?security_group_id={sg_id} — the API requires security_group_id as a required query param (confirmed live: 400 without, 200 with). No VPC needed — SGs are account/region-scoped. KEY FACTS (2026-06-20): listsecuritygrouprules requires security_group_id query param (required, not optional); setsecuritygroup body fields are {description, loggable} (name is NOT a valid setsecuritygroup field per request_example); showsecuritygrouprule needs a real rule_id (requires prior create-rule, covered by scenarios.json main lifecycle, not this fragment).

steps.name: set-sg
steps._note: setsecuritygroup body: {description, loggable} per api_docs request_example. 'name' is NOT a setsecuritygroup field (proven from docs: request_example only shows description+loggable). optional+broad expect_status so a 4xx still records without failing.

steps.name: list-rules
steps._note: Covers listsecuritygrouprules: security_group_id is REQUIRED query param (confirmed live 2026-06-20: 400 without it, 200 with real sg_id). A freshly created SG has no rules so response count:0, but the 200 still grants coverage credit.

steps.name: probe-sg-reads
steps._note: Auto-seed probe_reads: with sg_id in ctx, fires listsecuritygrouprules (required query param resolved from mapping). showsecuritygrouprule is NOT fired here because no rule_id is available (this lifecycle doesn't create rules — that is covered by the 'networking-security-group' lifecycle in scenarios.json which creates and captures rule_id).
